Public prepare_indices takes current optional manifest, owned current indices, config, optional decoded Arc ledger and settled FragReuseUpdate. Docs require per-attempt current state and explain inline decode versus unprefetched external rejection. It prepares in-place Update/Merge/DataReplacement coverage through lineage; it does not itself open external history. Missing read capability is not silently treated as no lineage by the called parser.

Run pure tagged write gate before cloning indices. With a current manifest compute rewritten physical columns; only nonempty rewrites construct TaggedLineage from original metadata/caller ledger, collect live fragment IDs using checked u32 conversion dropping out-of-range values, and withdraw coverage in cloned prepared list. Thus invalid ledger can remain unparsed when no physical rewrite is present. Current manifest and input index elements are not mutated; errors drop local clone.

Return PreparedIndices with optional current version, owned original Vec, cloned/adjusted Vec and settled FRI update. Public build_manifest forwards to build_manifest_with_read_version with None read state; no local operation validation or disk publication in wrapper. Signatures return an owned candidate Manifest plus owned final index list.

Public build_manifest_with_read_version takes optional borrowed ReadVersionState but prepares with no ledger and FragReuseUpdate::None, then calls prepared builder. External history rejection applies when preparation needs to decode it; tagged intent admission follows classifier, not a universal prohibition on every tagged operation. Documentation calls creation/detached cases None; API does not verify that read state corresponds to transaction.read_version.

Public build_manifest_prepared first compares prepared.manifest_version() to current Option version, rejecting mismatch with both values. Equality of version numbers is the only binding check here, not manifest content/UUID identity. Re-run gate against prepared original indices and settled FRI intent, then consume into_parts. Comments say publishes final list, but this synchronous builder returns metadata; actual storage publication occurs elsewhere.

If config requests stable IDs for existing nonstable table without migration_next_row_id, return NotSupported with migration advice. Independently collect names of every original index except exact FRI name; migration Some with any blockers errors, including MemWAL. This exclusion checks name only, not details/type. Creating migration config does not itself validate row IDs or apply publication. Conditions distinguish config request from already-active manifest flag.

Clone current base_paths or create empty map. Overwrite initial_bases Some is accepted only for dataset creation; loop rejects repeated IDs before inserting cloned BasePath entries. Existing dataset returns InvalidInput even for Some(empty), reiterating validation should have caught it. URI uniqueness, access and base resolution are not checked in this local registration step. All mutations are to local candidate map.

Select schema from Overwrite/Merge/Project payload, otherwise clone current schema or Internal if absent. Compute next fragment ID as current max_fragment_id()+1 or0; additions are ordinary arithmetic with no checked overflow here. Allocate empty final fragment Vec and take prepared indices. High-water-mark comment explains avoiding reused row-address/cache/deletion identity, but arbitrary supplied nonzero fragment IDs are not rejected by this setup.

Migration config removes all final indices named FRI. If any original MemWAL reserved-name entry existed, snapshot non-system CoverageIdentity sets from originals before preparation, otherwise skip cloning cost. Drop original metadata Vec afterward. This activation depends on original list; adding MemWAL for the first time does not enable this before/after hook in the same build.

Stable allocation state precedence: existing reader FLAG_STABLE_ROW_IDS always uses existing next_row_id even if config.use_stable_row_ids=false; new table plus true starts0; false otherwise uses None; existing nonstable plus true requires supplied migration next value or NotSupported. Migration_next_row_id Some with false does not independently activate this Option, although earlier migration-specific checks/removal still run. No validation of supplied migration watermark occurs here.

Prepare Result<&Vec<Fragment>> lazily from optional current manifest, with operation-name Internal error, then compute candidate version1 or current.version+1 unchecked. Operations consume the missing-manifest error only when using ?. Clone explicitly returns Internal that it should not enter builder. Operation validation and conflict resolution are not called by this section.

Append requires current fragments, clones/preserves them in order, allocates placeholder IDs for cloned new fragments, then when stable allocation active assigns row IDs and overwrites both created/update metadata from build_version_meta(new_version). Append new fragments afterward. Count/lineage preconditions and helper panic behavior remain those of assign_row_ids/build_version_meta; no actual file writes or schema mutation.

Delete constructs deleted-ID HashSet and updated-ID HashMap with last duplicate update winning. Clone current fragments, remove deleted IDs, then replace only deletion_file on surviving matching IDs. Other staged post-image fields are deliberately ignored to preserve rebased current overlays/files/lineage. Missing updated/deleted IDs have no direct error here; deletion wins if an ID is in both. Retain relevant indices against final fragments/schema.

Update borrows removed/updated/new fragments, modified fields, compacted SSTables, index-preservation fields, mode and offset map. Requires current fragments. Removed-ID set deduplicates; updated_by_id inserts with or_insert so first duplicate wins, unlike Delete. Build live schema field-ID set by preorder, including nested fields. None of these maps validates duplicate contradictions itself.

Scan current fragments in order. Remove listed IDs first. For each surviving updated ID clone staged post-image, replace overlays with current overlays, and prune staged base files that contain neither current schema fields nor the staged fragment's spilled lineage IDs. RewriteColumns mode tombstones overlays for fields_modified; other modes carry them intact. Unchanged fragments are current clones; updated payload IDs absent from current are ignored. Deletion/file/lineage state otherwise comes from staged post-image, not a full merge with current.

An empty if next_row_id.is_some block and comments do not stamp any metadata. Extend final_fragments with updated survivors. Partial latest-update stamping runs only with active stable allocation, explicit RewriteColumns, present nonempty offset map. For each final fragment require matching map entry, updated_by_id membership, nonempty bitmap and preexisting latest-update metadata; skipped cases remain unchanged. This prevents fabricating historical stamps for fragments lacking metadata.

For each eligible partial update, linearly find original physical_rows, using fallback1<<24 if missing. Reject bitmap cardinality greater than limit before rejecting maximum offset>=limit, with detailed values. Then collect sorted bitmap offsets as Vec<usize> and call partial refresh with new_version, previous current.version or0 and preloaded spilled lineage. Earlier candidate fragments may already be modified on failure, but candidate is local to this Result-returning builder. Helper may have additional count/decode errors; no IO performed here.

Coverage withdrawal already happened in prepare_indices. Clone new update fragments through placeholder ID iterator, prune their base files against current schema plus each new fragment's spilled IDs, assign missing row IDs when stable allocation active, then resolve created/latest metadata from original existing fragments and preloaded lineage. Ordering matters: resolver sees allocated IDs. A staged file retaining at least one live field stays whole; this pruning does not rewrite its field mapping.

Index reuse for RewriteRows tests config.use_stable_row_ids, not merely active next_row_id. Collect pure-update new fragment IDs, concatenate removed IDs plus every updated payload ID as source list, and build map of current overlaid source fragments keyed by unchecked u32 cast. Invoke register_pure_rewrite_rows_update_frags_in_indices with preservation fields/schema. It can error or modify candidate index coverage; existing source overlays are considered to avoid carrying stale values. A stable table with false config skips this optional reuse branch.

Call assign_row_ids a second time when stable allocation active, relying on existing metadata to avoid reallocating; preserve version metadata from resolver. Source comment's numeric line references1627-1755 are stale and do not define execution order. Build target_ids HashSet of new fragments but do not read it afterward in this arm, so it incurs allocation with no local semantic effect. Append new fragments, retain relevant indices, and only then strictly update nonempty MemWAL compacted markers with new_version; helper errors abort candidate return.

Overwrite clones only supplied fragments and overwrites every incoming fragment ID with sequential high-water IDs, including nonzero IDs. Ordinary increments unchecked. With stable allocation, assign missing row IDs and restamp both version metadata uniformly from new version. Replace final fragment list and discard every index. Carried-over fragment rejection is delegated to earlier validate_operation, not performed here; direct builder callers must respect that precondition.

Rewrite clones existing fragments then delegates handle_rewrite_fragments with groups, mutable fragment counter, current version and optional stable row watermark. Obtain optional TaggedRewriteAssembly only from prepared FragReuseUpdate::Rewrite. ordered_rewrite_groups excludes groups whose sources were reordered by stable-partition transitions so provenance remains on retired sources rather than falsely claiming destination coverage. Group intersection validation delegates helper.

With active stable IDs, debug_assert rewritten_indices empty (not a release error), skip indices recognized as FRI by name/details predicate, and transform each present bitmap. Row-address-domain indices drop ordered rewritten sources without following destinations; row-ID-domain indices recalculate source-to-destination coverage fallibly. Unknown bitmap None stays None. This path ignores provided rewritten-index replacements after the debug assertion and does not inspect row-map file contents.

Without stable IDs, handle_rewrite_indices applies rewritten metadata and ordered-group bitmap rules. In both branches prune overlay-stale index fields for every rewrite group afterward because fresh base data materializes overlays. These are in-memory metadata changes; no index files are copied, removed or rebuilt in this code.

If prepared assembly exists, select first current final FRI-name entry dataset_version and compare Option with assembly.base_entry_version; mismatch errors with both versions and commit-path advice. This is a consistency check, not CAS or proof of entire history identity; comments place concurrency protection in external per-attempt assembly/CAS. Retain entries whose name differs from assembly.entry.name and append cloned assembly entry, ignoring operation's own FRI payload. It validates neither assembly UUID nor full bytes here.

Without assembly, Some legacy FRI entry is spliced by removing all same-name indices and appending clone; no local byte decode, preserving existing snapshot behavior after gate. None does nothing. CreateIndex preserves current fragments, removes existing entries whose UUID appears in removed or new lists, validates covering fields on every new entry, then extends with clones in supplied order. No deduplication of repeated new UUID/name occurs here; validation failure only damages local candidate state.
